transcript.content: Hello, what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I guess the main reason I'm here is that I've just... I've stopped caring about everything I used to look forward to. 

My fishing gear is just sitting untouched out in the garage, gathering dust. I used to spend a lot of time in my woodshop, but now even the thought of going out there just feels like a massive chore. And, uh... even when my kids try to get me to sit down and play chess with them, I'm really just going through the motions. I just don't have any interest in things right now, and I don't know why.
Have you ever had a distinct period when you felt unusually high or irritable compared with your usual self?

No, I can't say that I have. I mean, I've never felt unusually high or... super energetic like that. I'm usually a pretty steady guy. As for being irritable, I mean, I get stressed at work sometimes, but nothing out of the ordinary. It's really just been the exact opposite of feeling high, to be honest.
How long have you been feeling this loss of interest in the things you usually enjoy?

It's been going on for about a year and seven months now. That was right around the time my wife started having health problems, and... well, it just changed everything at home. I haven't really had any interest in my normal stuff since then.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the day, nearly every day?

I don't know if "sad" is really the right word for it. I mean, I don't sit around crying or feeling heartbroken or anything like that. It's more just... flat. Like I just feel empty most of the day. I don't really feel much of anything at all, to be honest, just that complete lack of interest I was talking about.
Are your wife’s health problems still ongoing?
Yeah, they are. She's got this chronic autoimmune thing... it's just a constant battle. We're always managing it, going to appointments, trying different treatments. It hasn't really let up.
How has your energy level been since you began feeling this way?

It's been really low. Honestly, by midmorning, I feel like I’ve already worked a full twelve-hour shift. I'm out on sites a lot for work, and... well, even just walking the project or climbing stairs with the crew, it literally feels like my body is carrying wet concrete. I just don't have anything in the tank.
During the past year and seven months, has there been any period of at least two months when you felt like yourself again?

No, I haven't. It's been pretty constant this whole time. I mean, maybe there's a day here or there where the feeling is slightly less heavy, but definitely not two whole months. I haven't really felt like myself at all since this started.
How has your sleep been since this began?

It's been pretty bad, honestly. I can get into bed completely exhausted from the day, but then... I just lie there. My mind just keeps running through bills, the schedules for the sites, all of it. And if I do manage to fall asleep, I end up waking up around three or four in the morning. Then I just stare at the ceiling until it’s time to get up and drive to the site. It's like I can't shut it off.

{"intent":"Assess for a core depressive symptom that would help determine whether he meets criteria for a major depressive episode rather than adjustment disorder or persistent depressive disorder.","question":"Since this began, have you had trouble concentrating or making decisions?""}

Yeah, definitely. It's actually been a real problem on the job. I used to be able to keep all the schedules and the different subcontractors straight right in my head without even trying. But lately... I don't know, I'll find myself reading the exact same email three times before it actually registers. Or I'll be in a meeting with the guys and just completely forget what I was about to say. 

The decisions are the worst part, though. I just freeze up over things that used to take me five minutes to make a call on. It's like my brain just won't work.
Since this began, have you been feeling worthless or excessively guilty?

Yeah. I have. I just... I keep thinking I've completely failed my wife and my kids. And the guys at work, too. It feels like anytime anything goes wrong—like if there's a missed appointment, or a cost overrun on a project, or even a minor safety issue on site—I just take it as proof that I'm useless. I honestly feel like everyone would just be better off without me in charge.
Have you had thoughts about killing yourself or deliberately hurting yourself?

Yeah... I have. It happens mostly on those early drives to the site, before anyone else is really awake. I'll just be driving and... I catch myself thinking that it would just be easier if I didn't make it there. Sometimes the thought of just steering off the road crosses my mind. It actually scares me, honestly, because it feels a little too close.
